title: The Zscaler MCP server's ZCell tools: 20 reads, the customer ID, time windows, prompts and gaps

prose.text: The MCP server wraps the Python SDK's ZCell reads; toolsets and entitlement filtering are shared with other products ([[shared.mcp-server.tool-inventory]]), and whether the token's product value for Cellular is the one the filter expects is open in [[shared.mcp-server.tool-inventory:prd-alias-set]].

inventory.statement: The MCP server registers 20 ZCell tools, all read-only, and its tests assert both; its toolsets guide groups them into nine toolsets.

customer-id.statement: ZCell tools need `ZCELL_CUSTOMER_ID` in addition to the shared OneAPI credentials, separate from the `ZSCALER_CUSTOMER_ID` ZPA uses; the server injects it as `zcellCustomerId`, so it is not a tool parameter.

quotes: ZCell requires **one additional credential**: your Zscaler Cellular customer ID, supplied via the `ZCELL_CUSTOMER_ID` environment variable
This is separate from `ZSCALER_CUSTOMER_ID` (which ZPA uses) — set both if you use ZPA and ZCell together.
All other OneAPI credentials (`ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID`, `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET` / `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY`, `ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN`) are shared.
The ZCell customer id is NOT a tool parameter

missing-scope-error.statement: With `ZCELL_CUSTOMER_ID` unset, a ZCell tool fails saying the value is required for zcell tools, that it is the tenant or customer ID rather than an OneAPI credential so authentication is unaffected, and that it may not exist if the tenant is not entitled to the product.

prompts.statement: Three ZCell prompts are registered: `zcell_investigate_sim` (an ICCID, and a lookback defaulting to 7 days), `zcell_audit_data_usage` (lookback default 30 days, optional country) and `zcell_review_anomaly_policies` (lookback default 30 days, optional policy type); the anomaly review's workflow inventories the policies, gets the location groups of geofencing policies and lists each policy's violations and logs with the read-only `zcell_*` tools.

partial-toolset-prompts.statement: With only some ZCell toolsets selected, a ZCell prompt can be offered whose steps call tools that are not registered, for example the anomaly review's location-group lookup when `zcell_sim_location_groups` is not selected.
partial-toolset-prompts.conditions: Follows from prompt-gating (per service, not per tool) and the prompt text naming specific tools.

read-subset.statement: MCP exposes reads only: anomaly-policy create, update, delete and status changes, customer and region updates, SIM download, tag assignment, lock, status, eSIM assignment and eSIM state refresh, SIM location group writes, tag creation and tower-location history are reachable only through the SDK or raw API.
read-subset.conditions: Rests on inventory (20 read-only tools) compared against the operations in the generated zcell surface.

days-computed-where.summary: The MCP field description says the days window resolves on the server; the SDK computes it on the client.

days-computed-where.impact: The window follows the MCP host's clock; a skewed host shifts the window.

audit-blobs.summary: The audit tool's description says before and after data is omitted; its code returns the full SDK record, which includes it.

audit-blobs.impact: Audit rows can be larger than the description suggests and do include the change data an investigation needs.

audit-object-id.impact: Whether the backend coerces a string object ID is unknown; the entry ID, root customer and sort filters cannot be used from MCP at all.

audit-request.title: Audit search typing and the filters MCP leaves out
audit-request.detail: MCP sends object_id as a string and omits the contract's entry id, root customerId and sortBy/sortDir inputs. Whether the backend accepts the string form, and whether the omissions are intended narrowing, is not established.
